finding.claim: big5 recognizer accepts heads 0xA1-0xFE, but the server treats only 0xA1-0xF9 as heads; writeBufferEscapeMb copies head+trail pairs verbatim, so an attacker Buffer parameter [0xFA,0x5C,0x27] is emitted as FA 5C 5C 27, leaving a bare quote that closes the _BINARY literal (SQL injection). Confidence medium: server big5 head range is from recollection, not verified against a live server.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled bytes in a Buffer value bound as a placeholder in a text-protocol query (connection.query with ? and Buffer param) on a connection with charset big5
finding.sink: _BINARY '...' literal emitted by writeBufferEscape in the text protocol

trace.note: valid pair copied verbatim: FA 5C emitted with no escape

finding.guards_checked: Backslash-mode branch not taken (noBackslashEscapes false in backslash mode); lone-head escape only when mbLen<2; quote/backslash escape applies to non-head bytes; string path (escapeString in utils.js) escapes per char and is unaffected; gbk/sjis/cp932/gb18030 recognizers match server ranges as recalled.

finding.claim: Pool.escape picks session escape mode via _searchInfo, whose active-connection loop iterates Object.keys indices ('0','1',...) instead of connection thread IDs. The lookup almost always returns undefined, so info is null and the backslash escape map is used even when the server runs with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, making a quote injectable.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled string passed to pool.escape(value) and placed inside a single-quoted SQL literal
finding.sink: SQL string literal executed on a connection in NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES mode

trace.note: idleConnections.get(0) empty when all connections are busy or none idle
activeConnections['0'] is undefined, so conn is undefined
backslash LITTERAL_ESCAPE map selected; quote becomes \'
escaped output emitted; under NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES the backslash-quote closes the literal

finding.guards_checked: connection.escape/format use per-connection info (connection.js:113) and are correct; pool.query runs on a real connection; escapeId doubles backticks and ignores mode; when an idle connection exists the head connection's mode is used, which is wrong only if session modes differ.
